items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: He had some old records of Lee Collins, sounded real good on those

ctx.x: The old violin player. He used to play at the Lyric Theater when I heard it. I couldn't even go there. I was a kid then, around 18, 19, 20. I mean I've heard about him and Joe has told me plenty about it. But he has helped Joe a lot too. But still, Joe has stayed within that same track. He hasn't moved. I doubted Joe is a better piano player now than he was in 1925. See, because he never would try to improve himself. But he was a good piano player.
But I mean, I would- He had some old records of Lee Collins, sounded real good on those, back 1928 or 1909. Yeah.

But now, I wouldn't dare put Joe in a class with Steve, or even Walter Pichon. Walter Pichon was another genius. Well, he stayed and he kept practicing until he made something out of it. Now, I had- At one time we had some records in there. We promised to try to copy them, but we were going to get somebody to write down the melodies of them and see if we could get an arrangement on them for about a six piece and play them.
